title: The letters of aerea, set as spokes round a single r
description: Five letters on a square grid, read through one r at the centre: every spoke reads e then a outward, so every line through the middle spells aerea; with three letters the cross reads are across and era down. Each cell is as wide as the average letter plus a gap the size of the face’s own letter spacing, so the ink sits the same distance apart across and down. In stop motion at 12 frames a second a cross turns round the grid, the e’s a frame ahead of the a’s, or the spokes open and clear from the centre out; three stills hold the cross, the diagonal and the eight spokes, the r fixed at the centre in each.
colophon: PP Kyoto Medium by Pangram Pangram Foundry, used when it is in fonts/trial (free for personal use); Instrument Serif otherwise.
Letter outlines read with fontkit; drawn on Canvas 2D, frames paced by counting screen refreshes so every one is held equally.

title: Hiragana, katakana and Latin glyphs, set as one block of type
description: One block of type set edge to edge in a single size. A map of organic shapes sits underneath: as each line is set, the shape under the cursor decides whether it repeats a glyph, steps through a letter's accents or carries running copy. Sections meet at a single word space.
colophon: PP Kyoto by Pangram Pangram Foundry. Extrabold for the patterns, Medium for the copy. Free for personal use.
Glyph outlines read with fontkit, set on Canvas 2D; shapes from simplex noise.

title: Letters, kana and shapes built from a square grid
hint: Move over the poster to look closer, click for another arrangement
description: Each form is set on a grid of cells and cut into patches that grow along its strokes. Every cell is then drawn from a small vocabulary. Eight studies take one reference each; eleven combinations cross them in other typefaces and brighter inks; seven emblems, on black, build objects from perforated, stitched and oval cells with their names knocked out of them, between stitched ornaments.
colophon: PP Kyoto (Pangram Pangram); Haffer, Reckless, Post and Coxx (Displaay); ABC Areal (Dinamo), all trials or free for personal use. Bricolage Grotesque and Roboto Flex, open source.
Glyph outlines read with fontkit (or drawn by the browser for variable WOFF2 fonts) and sampled onto the grid; drawn on Canvas 2D.

title: Pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis, spelled as a web of letters
description: A long word spelled as a diagram. Every letter it uses is set once, and every time one letter follows another an arrow runs between them, so the letters it keeps returning to gather arrows. Packets of color run the word’s path all at once and never stop: each leaves its letter in that letter’s color, turns into the next one’s as it travels and fades back into the white web; the letter flares as it arrives and sends it on. From the last letter the path runs back to the first, so it loops with no restart.
colophon: Pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis, a lung disease from fine volcanic dust, coined in 1935 to be the longest word in English dictionaries; twelve more long words to choose from, each with its own layouts.
Söhne Mono Buch by Klim Type Foundry, trial. JetBrains Mono when it isn’t installed.
Bloom, read from the pixels of a glossy rainbow knot: cobalt, aqua, gold, orange, red, magenta, lilac.

Canvas 2D. Letters placed by simulated annealing for few crossings, room round each letter and every two arrow ends at a letter at least 26° apart; a layout is kept only when its drawn lines cross but never overlap or nearly touch.

title: Sen, a line typeface for kanji with width and weight axes
hint: Space pauses. In Axes, move over the grid to set width and weight
description: A typeface drawn only in lines. Each kanji and kana starts as the centre of a brush stroke; the curve is simplified to a few straight lines, near-level strokes are set level and near-upright ones upright, the hooks are cut and the dots become short dashes. Two axes move it: width stretches the skeleton from narrow to wide while the line stays the same, and weight thickens the one line from a hairline to a heavy pen. The copy is the opening of the Japanese Wikipedia article on kanji.
colophon: 漢字 (Kanji), Japanese Wikipedia: five sentences from the opening, set as written. CC BY-SA 4.0.
KanjiVG stroke centrelines by Ulrich Apel, CC BY-SA 3.0, redrawn as straight lines.
Width 50–125, weight 100–900: a line 1% to 9% of the em.
Canvas 2D. Fraunces Italic and JetBrains Mono for the Latin.

title: Lines of On Growth and Form in round rings, drifting, with bursts
description: Six rings of type nested about one centre, each tall at one end and small at the other, run off the edges of the square. They never stop: each turns steadily, inner rings faster, alternate rings the other way, its shape breathing slowly. Every 0.7 to 1.5 seconds one to three neighbouring rings snap round in under a second, eased very sharply, often swapping their tall end through a tall middle, and the view zooms in or out with them, so the snap and the zoom land together. Each ring keeps its words through every change, and no ring ever grows tall enough to touch the next.
colophon: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1917), chapter XI, The Logarithmic Spiral, from its first line, set in capitals. Public domain, from Project Gutenberg.
Instrument Serif by Rodrigo Fuenzalida and Jordan Egstad, Instrument, spaced 0.02 em. SIL Open Font License.
Ink from #cdd2d9 at each ring’s start to #7d8794 at its end, cool greys, on black.
Glyph outlines read with opentype.js and laid flat once; a WebGL vertex shader bends them onto each ring on every frame, with motion blur from a 180 degree shutter.

title: Forty glyphs drawn in ovals that grow from a grid of dots
hint: Press → for the next glyph, ← for the last, space to pause
description: Each glyph is sampled onto a 24 by 24 grid, all at one size and centred on its own ink. Every cell is one white oval: its size follows how much of the cell the glyph covers, and it turns to lie along the stroke. Between glyphs each oval that changes pulls back into its grid dot, then springs out as the next glyph, overshooting a little before it settles; the next change begins the moment the last oval lands.
colophon: Geist by Vercel, Extrabold and Regular, under the SIL Open Font License.
Glyph outlines read with fontkit and sampled onto the grid once, with each cell's stroke direction from its structure tensor; drawn on Canvas 2D in Display P3 with damped springs.

title: Two kanji drawn as one line, with every point and coordinate as four axes move
description: 龍 (dragon) over 驚 (surprise), each drawn as a single line through the centre of Noto Sans JP, with the fewest points that keep every curve smooth. Every point, handle and coordinate stays on show while four axes move on their own periods: weight from a hairline to a heavy pen, width from narrow to twice as wide, corners from sharp to fully round, and slant, which gives way as the letters widen. The readouts on the right are the axes' values, not controls.
colophon: Centre lines of Noto Sans JP Thin by Google, SIL Open Font License 1.1, found by thinning its outlines; curves fitted with Hobby's method, as in METAFONT.
Units of the em, 1000, with y up from the baseline.
SVG, redrawn each frame. Inter Tight and JetBrains Mono for the readouts.

title: A year of dates poured into one shape, its blocks sliding like falling pieces
hint: Space starts or stops the motion, ← and → change the year
description: Every month opens with its first three letters, then its days, one to a cell, set edge to edge in one size and in black on a bright block of color. The days sit under their weekdays, Sunday to Saturday, in three bands of four months; each month starts a new row, so the holes are where its first and last weeks don't reach and every year has its own shape. Each beat a few runs of rows or columns slide one to four cells at once, snap into place and wrap around the sheet; after nine beats the moves play back and the calendar puts itself together again.
colophon: PP Right Serif Mono and PP Kyoto by Pangram Pangram Foundry, used when installed (free for personal use); JetBrains Mono otherwise.
One OKLCH hue a month, pushed to the edge of the screen's gamut at a light step so black stays readable.
Canvas 2D; the moves are seeded and played back exactly, with a quint in-out ease.

title: Squares on a turning torus, one warm colour a row, each counting 0 to 9
description: A grid of squares, ten rows of sixteen, is wrapped onto a horn torus: a ring whose hole closes to a point. Every square counts 0 to 9 and round again, each starting on a different digit from its neighbours, and the new digit rolls up into the square on the beat while the rows roll up the tube a square at a time. Each digit's outline is warped through the surface point by point, not pasted on flat. At rest the torus sits at the isometric angle; it turns sideways like a turntable, end over end, or both at once.
colophon: PP Neue Corp Extended Medium by Pangram Pangram Foundry, used when it is in fonts/trial (free for personal use); Roboto Flex at its widest otherwise.
One ink a row in a loop of OKLCH tones at a similar lightness: salmon, pink, red and orange, back to salmon, on white with black digits and hairline gaps.
Digit outlines read with fontkit and flattened once; drawn on Canvas 2D with perspective, back faces painted first so the outline stays whole, quintic easing.

title: Lowercase e’s stretched into ellipses, flowing from a centre and mirrored four ways
description: Each token is an ellipse with a lowercase e stretched inside it, its ink an even gap from the edge on every side. Tokens sit at geometric radii along spokes and travel outward, growing from nothing as they leave the eye at the centre and shrinking away at the rim; in counterflow neighbouring spokes run in opposite directions. One quadrant is drawn from a rule and its layout is reflected, or turned a quarter at a time, into the other three, but the glyphs never are: every e is redrawn upright where it lands. Flow never stops, easing between a fast and a slow pace, and every speed loops seamlessly in eight seconds.
colophon: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next Bold by the Braille Institute, designed by Applied Design Works, under the SIL Open Font License, via Fontsource.
Light: saturated pink ellipses on pale pink with black lines and glyphs. Dark: black on black with pink lines and glyphs.
Canvas 2D; each e's ink box measured with measureText and scaled to fill its ellipse.
